correctness.rationale: For G_n=K_1 vee (K_{n,n}-M_n), every deleted-matching pair a_i,b_i has a unique length-two geodesic with hub h internal. A dual set X containing h therefore must split each such pair exactly once; otherwise a_i,b_i on either same side of X cannot be X-visible. With p selected A endpoints and q=n-p selected B endpoints, selected A-A pairs can avoid X internally only through some unselected b_k, k distinct from both endpoints; this is automatic at p<=1 and possible for all pairs iff p>=3, hence p!=2. Similarly q!=2. Outside A-A pairs require p>=1 and outside B-B pairs q>=1, while adjacent cross-shore pairs need no intermediary. Conversely these four conditions suffice, proving exact binomial count. Every admissible X yields dual complement Y because h is outside Y and every nonadjacent Y-pair has an unblocked length-two geodesic via h, so chi_dual<=2. Entire V(G_n) is not dual since a matching nonedge needs blocked hub. Existence n=2 or n>=4 (p=1), impossibility n=3, completes all n>=2. The source verifier was fetched from its actual Git blob, SHA-verified and executed for n=2..8 (87,376 hub-containing subsets); a separately coded generic BFS-geodesic visibility checker independently exhausted all hub-containing subsets for n=2..7, agreeing exactly. Finite checks corroborate rather than prove arbitrary n.
residual_risks: The result does not classify cones of arbitrary graphs or dual-set colorings not in this family; counts refer exactly to hub-containing sets.
Boundary case n=2 is a disconnected crown before coning but resulting G_n is connected and proof remains valid.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality attaches only to the uniform structural characterization of hub-containing dual sets, exact binomial count, and characterization of the unique non-2-colorable crown-cone parameter n=3. The initiating 2026 paper explicitly supplies the n=3 wheel C_6 vee K_1 as known prior coverage, which is not new. Its Theorem 4 only gives sufficient obstructions to infinite dual coloring, not the all-n crown-cone finite side. The 2025 dual visibility polynomials paper computes dual sets of K_{n,n} without matching deletion/coning. A published complete-multipartite dual-coloring classification does not cover G_n: for n>=3 its nonadjacency relation is not transitive (a1 nonadjacent to a2 and b1, but a2 adjacent to b1), so it is not complete multipartite. A 2024 diameter-two visibility paper studies extremal set cardinalities rather than coloring partitions. Search hits on crowns concern unrelated coloring and domination invariants. Residual risk remains of an unindexed equivalent cone result in this very recent literature.
residual_risks: Very recent 2026 origins can have newly posted or unindexed crown-cone results under uncommon aliases; absence from search is not priority proof.
The n=3 wheel obstruction is explicitly published and not novel; classification/count for all n and particularly n>=4 are the only accepted originality contribution.
Combinatorial restriction p,q !=2 is elementary after the geodesic split, so extent of standalone novelty is limited.

value.rationale: This is a natural infinite family directly generalizing the initiating paper's conspicuous previously known noncolorable wheel C6 vee K1. It completely determines a graph-invariant transition which is not monotone in n (no coloring at n=3, two classes for all n>=4), rather than merely checking a handful of instances. The exact classification of all hub-containing dual sets and closed binomial count explain the structural mechanism and can support future work on visibility partitions of graph cones. The fact concerns a canonical matched-edge-deleted complete bipartite family and is not an arbitrary finite slice; the known n=3 exception is credited and the claim is not inflated into a characterization of arbitrary cones or diameter-two graphs.
residual_risks: Specialized family and easy binomial enumeration after the structural lemma limit breadth; no general cone characterization follows.
No claim of improvement in general dual-coloring algorithms or complexity.

limitations: Only n>=2 crown-cone graphs with one universal hub; cannot infer results for arbitrary joins, cones or diameter-two graphs.
The n=3 wheel obstruction was previously published in arXiv:2609.31427v1.
Finite verified n=2..8 does not prove infinite claim; correctness rests on exact geodesic proof.
Originality best-of-knowledge, not a historical-priority certificate; no independent formal Lean proof or human expert attestation is claimed.
